claims: April Fools' Day is celebrated on April 1.
France adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1582.
King Charles IX adopted the Gregorian calendar.
King Charles IX changed the New Year from April 1 to January 1.
People who forgot or were slow to learn of the 1582 calendar change in France continued celebrating in late March or April 1.
People who forgot or were slow to learn of the 1582 calendar change in France were mocked.
People who forgot or were slow to learn of the 1582 calendar change in France received fake gifts.
People who forgot or were slow to learn of the 1582 calendar change in France were sent on fool's errands.
Hilaria is an ancient Roman festival in late March.
Some historians trace April Fools' Day to the ancient Roman festival of Hilaria.
During Hilaria, people dressed in disguises.
During Hilaria, people mocked one another.
Poisson d'Avril is a common tradition in France.
Poisson d'Avril involves taping a paper fish to someone's back.
Poisson d'Avril has been popular in Europe from the 16th century onward
